data.name: Usage
data.value:
Usage: Latiprimere.Cli list Latiprimere.Cli caps <printer-id> Latiprimere.Cli print-capabilities <printer-id> [--ticket FILE | --default-ticket] Latiprimere.Cli print <printer-id> <file> [--raw] [--copies N] [--duplex one|long|short] [--landscape] [--cancel] [--output FILE] [--stats] [--paper NAME] [--color color|mono] [--tray ID] [--option KEY=VALUE]... [--ticket FILE] [--pages LIST] [--quality draft|normal|high]
Files ending .png, .jpg or .jpeg are sent as images, .txt as UTF-8 text, others as PDF, unless --raw is given. --cancel cancels the job straight after submitting it. --output prints to FILE instead of the device (Windows printers only). --stats reports time and memory used. --paper and --tray take a paper size's name (such as iso_a4_210x297mm) and a tray's ID, as caps lists them. --pages prints only the pages listed, such as 1-3,5, counted from 1. A PDF with a password is opened with the one in LATIPRIMERE_PDF_PASSWORD. --option sets a vendor option, such as ipp:number-up=2; repeat it for more. caps lists the printer's vendor options with their values. --ticket sends a Print Ticket file as windows:print-ticket (Windows printers only). print-capabilities writes a Windows printer driver's Print Capabilities as XML, for the defaults with any --ticket FILE merged on, or with --default-ticket its default Print Ticket. Set CUPS_SERVER (for example localhost:631) to use a CUPS server from Windows. IPP printers on the network are found automatically and listed by name; quote IDs with spaces, for example "ipp:dnssd:Office Laser". List other printers in LATIPRIMERE_IPP_PRINTERS (comma-separated URIs, for example ipp://192.168.1.20/ipp/print). Trust the certificates of printers reached over ipps:// by listing their SHA-256 fingerprints, checked against each printer's own web page, in LATIPRIMERE_IPP_FINGERPRINTS (comma-separated).

data.name: PrintersHeading
data.comment: Heading above the printer list.

data.name: PrinterLine
data.comment: {0} is the printer name, {1} is the default marker or empty, {2} is the printer ID, {3} is the printer state.

data.name: PrinterDetailLine
data.comment: {0} is the printer description, location or make and model.

data.name: DefaultMarker
data.comment: Shown after the default printer's name.

data.name: PrintingUnavailable
data.comment: {0} is the reason, from the exception message.

data.name: PrintFailed
data.comment: {0} is the reason, from the exception message.

data.name: NativeErrorCode
data.comment: {0} is the native error code.

data.name: JobSubmitted
data.comment: {0} is the job ID, {1} is the printer name.

data.name: JobCancelRequested
data.comment: {0} is the job ID.

data.name: JobAlreadyFinished
data.value: Job {0} had already finished, so there was nothing to cancel.
data.comment: {0} is the job ID.

data.name: JobStatusLine
data.comment: {0} is the time, {1} the job state, {2} the state message part (or empty), {3} the state reasons part (or empty), {4} the pages part (or empty).

data.name: JobStatusMessagePart
data.comment: {0} is the job state message.

data.name: JobStatusReasonsPart
data.comment: {0} is the job's state reasons, comma-separated job-state-reasons keywords.

data.name: TrustCertificateHint
data.value: To trust this printer, check that the fingerprint matches the one on its own web page, then list it in {0}: {0}={1}
data.comment: {0} is the environment variable, {1} the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint.

data.name: JobStatusPagesPart
data.comment: {0} is the number of pages completed.

data.name: Statistics
data.value: Submitted in {0:F2} s, finished after {1:F2} s. Peak working set {2:F0} MiB; managed heap {3:F0} MiB.
data.comment: {0} submit seconds, {1} total seconds, {2} peak working set, {3} managed heap size.

data.name: InvalidArguments
data.comment: {0} describes the problem.

data.name: MissingPrintArguments
data.value: print needs a printer ID and a file.

data.name: MissingPrintCapabilitiesArguments
data.value: print-capabilities needs a printer ID, then --ticket FILE or --default-ticket, not both.

data.name: IppPrinterUriInvalid
data.value: {0} has '{1}', which isn't an absolute ipp:// or ipps:// address, such as ipp://192.168.1.20/ipp/print.
data.comment: {0} is the environment variable, {1} the value in it that isn't an address.

data.name: FileUnreadable
data.comment: {0} is the reason, from the exception message, which names the file.

data.name: NotAWindowsPrinter
data.value: {0} isn't a Windows printer. Print Capabilities and Print Tickets come from Windows printer drivers; caps lists every printer's vendor options.
data.comment: {0} is the printer ID.

data.name: VendorOptionLine
data.comment: {0} is the option's key, {1} its display name, {2} its values.

data.name: VendorChoiceValue
data.comment: {0} is the value to set, {1} its display name.

data.name: VendorNumberValue
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the limits; a missing one is shown as …

data.name: CapabilitiesHeading
data.comment: {0} is the printer name, {1} is the printer ID.

data.name: CapabilityLine
data.comment: {0} is the capability label, {1} its values.

data.name: PaperSizeValue
data.comment: {0} is the paper's display name, {1} its PWG name.

data.name: CustomSizeValue
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the narrowest and widest, {2} and {3} the shortest and longest, in millimetres.

data.name: RollSizeValue
data.comment: As CustomSizeValue, for a roll: the length is how much is cut from it.

data.name: NamedValue
data.comment: {0} is a media type's or output bin's name, {1} its print-system identifier.

data.name: MaxCopiesValue
data.comment: {0} is the most copies a job can ask for.

data.name: TrayValue
data.comment: {0} is the tray name, {1} its print-system identifier.

data.name: UnknownOption
data.comment: {0} is the option.

data.name: PaperNotListed
data.value: {0} doesn't list the paper size '{1}'. Run caps to see the sizes it has.
data.comment: {0} is the printer name, {1} the paper size's name.

data.name: TrayNotListed
data.value: {0} doesn't list the tray '{1}'. Run caps to see the trays it has.
data.comment: {0} is the printer name, {1} the tray ID.

data.name: InvalidOptionValue
data.value: '{0}' is not a valid value for {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the value, {1} is the option.
